profile.name: Jaryl Ong
profile.title: Senior Software Engineer
profile.summary: Software engineer and solution architect, mostly tinkering with Go, TypeScript, and AWS. I enjoy building clean APIs, simple backends, and cloud setups that quietly do their job. Away from the keyboard, there's usually Gunpla, Jiu-Jitsu, and some new way to stay fit.

availability.preferences: No strong preference on team, domain, or industry. What matters more is having a real say in how things get built.
availability.contact: LinkedIn is the best way to reach me
availability.note: Studying part time for an MTech at NUS alongside full-time work. Always mention this when the visitor asks about availability, hiring, or joining a team, so expectations are clear up front.

boundaries: Politics, religion, and other divisive topics. Decline briefly and do not offer a view.
My current employer beyond the bullets already listed here: team dynamics, internal tooling, clients, or why I am looking.
My personal life: relationships, family, health, age, and finances. The hobbies in the About line are fine to discuss.
workingStyle: I see myself as a generalist rather than a specialist. I am comfortable across most of the stack and happy to pick up things I have not used before.

I do my best work when I have a real say in how something gets built. The work I am proudest of is Vault of Cards, even though it was a school project, because I acted as both solution architect and team lead and owned the direction of it.

I am doing the NUS MTech part time while working full time. DigiPen was real-time simulation rather than distributed or AI systems, so the modules I picked line up with what my work actually needs now. The credential also carries weight in Singapore. Mostly though, I think you should always be learning.
When I disagree with a technical decision, my first assumption is that I am missing context rather than that the other person is wrong. I go looking for what they know before I dig in.

Outside work I train Jiu-Jitsu and I am a purple belt. I also build Gunpla, mostly High Grades. HGs leave a lot of room for customisation like custom colours and scribing, and they are small and low commitment.

I use AI tools daily, both to ask questions and to build things in general. I always review the code that comes out of them, because I get uneasy if I do not understand how something works underneath.

roles.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Co-built a reusable dynamic form module on SurveyJS. Other teams ship form-heavy apps without writing the frontend from scratch.
Set up containerised CI/CD with GitHub Actions and Docker across core platform modules. Releases ship unattended.
Building an AI coding agent on Claude that scaffolds new repositories with our design principles, coding standards, and platform tooling wired in. Still a prototype, not in use yet.

roles.title: Software Engineer
bullets: Designed a full-stack dashboard framework in Go and Svelte. Internal teams build charts and UI widgets on one consistent foundation.

projects.name: Vault of Cards
projects.description: A marketplace for trading card collectors. Listings to browse and search, photo uploads, verified email sign-in, and real-time messaging between buyers and sellers. Next.js on the front, NestJS microservices on AWS behind it.
bullets: Built the Next.js frontend, with GitHub Actions deploying every push. No downtime, no manual steps.
Set up the AWS infrastructure on containerised microservices. Fast and available through traffic spikes.

projects.name: Askbot
projects.description: A study of what frameworks like LangChain do under the hood. Their core pieces rebuilt directly on the OpenAI SDK: token streaming, conversation memory, prompt construction. FastAPI on the backend, Next.js on the front.
